{{Short description|British restaurant group}} {{Use dmy dates|date=June 2017}} {{Infobox company | name = The Big Table Group Limited | logo = | type = [[Privately held company|Private]] | founded = {{start date and age|2014|df=yes}} | hq_location = [[London]], England | key_people = Rooney Anand, non-executive chairman
James Spragg, CEO | area_served = [[United Kingdom]] | industry = [[Hospitality]] | products = | owner = Epiris | num_employees = | website = [https://www.bigtablegroup.com www.bigtablegroup.com] | footnotes = }} '''The Big Table Group Limited''', formerly '''Tragus Group''' and '''Casual Dining Group (CDG)''', is a hospitality company in the United Kingdom. The Big Table operates restaurants primarily under the [[Bella Italia]], [[Café Rouge]], [[Frankie & Benny's]] and [[Las Iguanas]] names. It also operates sites under the Banana Tree, [[Chiquito (restaurant)|Chiquito]], [[Coast to Coast (restaurant)|Coast to Coast]], Firejacks and Filling Station brands. It is owned by Epiris. In mid-May 2020, CDG warned its chains were at risk of going into [[administration (law)|administration]] but was later in talks with "multiple parties" about a sale of the business.{{Cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/business/2020/may/18/boparan-group-set-to-buy-carluccios-restaurants|title=Bella Italia owner set to bring in administrators, 6,000 jobs at risk|first=Sarah|last=Butler|date=18 May 2020|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]}} On 2 July 2020, it was announced that the company had been placed into administration, with 91 outlets set to close with the loss of 1,900 jobs.{{cite news |title=Café Rouge and Bella Italia owner falls into administration |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/business-53270679 |accessdate=2 July 2020 |publisher=[[BBC News]]}} Epiris brought CDG out of administration in August 2020, renaming it to The Big Table Group. ==History== ===Tragus Group=== Tragus Holdings was formed in 2002{{cite web|title=Tragus Holdings - Company Profile|url=http://www.caterersearch.com/Companies/33940/tragus-holdings.html|publisher=Caterer and Hotelkeeper|accessdate=23 November 2012|archive-date=6 July 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110706010842/http://www.caterersearch.com/Companies/33940/tragus-holdings.html|url-status=dead}}{{cite web|url=https://www.ft.com/content/af7fd470-ab78-11e3-8cae-00144feab7de|title=Apollo-led group set to take control of Tragus from Blackstone|last=Chassany|first=Anne-Sylvaine|date=14 March 2014|website=[[Financial Times]]|access-date=31 May 2017}} when [[Whitbread]] sold-off 153 failing restaurants from its Pelican and BrightReasons divisions, shortly after writing their value down by £147m.{{cite web|last=Osborne|first=Alistair|title=Cafe Rouge buy-in team nets £18m|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/finance/2903873/Cafe-Rouge-buy-in-team-nets-18m.html|publisher=[[The Daily Telegraph]]|accessdate=23 November 2012}} At the time, the two restaurant divisions comprised the Café Rouge, Bella Pasta, Mamma Amalfi, Abbaye, Leadenhall Wine Bar and Oriel brands. A £25m{{Cite news|url=https://www.standard.co.uk/news/whitbread-sells-restaurant-groups-6299454.html|title=Whitbread sells restaurant groups|date=31 May 2002|work=[[Evening Standard]]|access-date=31 May 2017|language=en-GB}} [[management buy-in]] by Tragus Holdings was funded by £11m from venture capitalist speculators [[ECI Partners]].{{cite web|last=Smiddy|first=Oliver|title=Case study: Tragus satisfies hunger for returns|url=http://www.efinancialnews.com/story/2007-08-06/case-study-tragus-satisfies-hunger-for-returns|publisher=eFinancial News|accessdate=23 November 2012}} Tragus Holdings was led by chief executive Finlay Scott, formerly head of the [[Aroma Café]] chain and Whitecross Dental Care. The team included Gavin Williams, managing director of Bella Pasta, and Harry Morley, former finance director of Whitecross Dental Care. In January 2005, Tragus' directors sold the company to [[Legal & General]] for £90m-£95m.{{cite web|url=https://www.thecaterer.com/articles/56888/lgv-buys-tragus-for-more-than-16390m|title=LGV buys Tragus for more than £90m|date=18 January 2005|website=The Caterer|access-date=31 May 2017}}{{cite web|title=LGV buys Tragus for more than £90m|date=18 January 2005 |url=http://www.caterersearch.com/Articles/21/04/2005/56888/LGV-buys-Tragus-for-more-than-16390m.htm|publisher=Caterer and Hotelkeeper|accessdate=23 November 2012}} The sale made them around £18m profit. The chairman, discredited former LSE CEO Gavin Casey, received £2m. Legal & General installed a new management team which included appointing new [[chief executive]] Graham Turner (formerly [[managing director]] of the [[Unique Pub Company]]).{{cite web|title=Caterer and Hotelkeeper 100: Graham Turner, Tragus|date=July 2011 |url=http://www.caterersearch.com/Articles/01/07/2011/339055/Caterer-and-Hotelkeeper-100-Graham-Turner-Tragus.htm|publisher=Caterer and Hotelkeeper|accessdate=26 November 2012}} In December 2006, Tragus was bought by [[Blackstone Group]] for £267m. By that time, the business had grown to 163 restaurants.{{cite web|url=https://www.thecaterer.com/articles/310517/caf-rouge-owner-tragus-bought-by-blackstone-group|title=Café Rouge owner Tragus bought by Blackstone Group|last=Druce|first=Chris|date=15 December 2006|website=The Caterer|access-date=31 May 2017}} In September 2006 it had also announced plans for a new restaurant concept - Huxley's Bar & Kitchen – to open in the new [[Heathrow Terminal 5]] in March 2008.{{cite news |title=Huxley's Bar & Kitchen – which opened in the new Heathrow Terminal 5 |url=https://www.bighospitality.co.uk/Article/2006/09/17/Tragus-to-launch-new-restaurant-concept-at-Heathrow |accessdate=29 May 2020 |work=Big Hospitality |date=16 September 2006}} The group expanded rapidly in 2007 with the purchase of Ma Potters restaurant company in February for £14.15m,{{cite web|title=Tragus buys Ma Potters restaurant company|url=http://www.bighospitality.co.uk/Business/Tragus-buys-Ma-Potters-restaurant-company|publisher=Big Hospitality|accessdate=23 November 2012}} and the [[Strada]] chain - which included five [[Belgo]] and Bierodrome restaurants - in May for £140m.{{cite web|last=Jones|first=Marc|title=Cafe Rouge owner Tragus swallows Strada|url=http://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-tragus-strada-idUKL3131616220070531|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160306152000/http://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-tragus-strada-idUKL3131616220070531|url-status=dead|archive-date=6 March 2016|publisher=Reuters|accessdate=23 November 2012}} In July, Tragus signed a deal with [[Center Parcs UK and Ireland|Center Parcs]] to operate several Bella Italia and Café Rouge restaurants in the leisure village operator's UK sites.{{cite web|url=https://www.thecaterer.com/articles/314937/bella-italia-and-caf-rouge-owner-tragus-signs-deal-with-center-parcs|title=Bella Italia and Café Rouge owner Tragus signs deal with Center Parcs|last=Walton|first=Christopher|date=17 July 2007|website=The Caterer|access-date=31 May 2017}} In April 2012 it was announced that Graham Turner would step down as Tragus chief executive. John Derkach, formerly managing director of the [[Costa Coffee]] chain took up the position in August 2012.{{cite web|title=Costa boss Derkach moves to head up Tragus|url=http://www.peach-report.com/Latest/1308007/costa_boss_derkach_moves_to_head_up_tragus.html|publisher=Peach Report|accessdate=26 November 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120718230619/http://www.peach-report.com/Latest/1308007/costa_boss_derkach_moves_to_head_up_tragus.html|archive-date=18 July 2012|url-status=dead}} In early 2014, Blackstone's stake in Tragus was acquired by US investor [[Apollo Global Management]],{{cite news |last1=Chassany |first1=Anne-Silvaine |last2=Robinson |first2=Duncan |title=Apollo-led group set to take control of Tragus from Blackstone |url=https://www.ft.com/content/af7fd470-ab78-11e3-8cae-00144feab7de |accessdate=8 June 2020 |work=Financial Times |date=14 March 2014}} and, in June 2014, Apollo sought to shed or restructure some of Tragus Group's rent obligations at Cafe Rouge and Bella Italia, and to sell its Strada chain.{{cite news |last1=Kleinman |first1=Mark |title=Cafe Rouge Owner To Offload Loss-Making Sites |url=https://news.sky.com/story/cafe-rouge-owner-to-offload-loss-making-sites-10402563 |accessdate=29 May 2020 |work=Sky News |date=3 June 2014}} In September 2014, Tragus sold Strada to Sun Capital Partners.{{cite web|last1=Michel|first1=Melodie|title=Strada sold to Sun Capital Partners for £37m|url=http://www.bighospitality.co.uk/Business/Strada-sold-to-Sun-Capital-Partners-for-37m|website=Big Hospitality|publisher=Willam Reed|accessdate=2 March 2017}} ===Casual Dining Group=== [[File:Bella Italia, Briggate, Leeds (30th March 2013).JPG|thumb|Bella Italia on [[Briggate]] in [[Leeds]]. Bella Italia is one of The Big Table's brands.]] In March 2015, Tragus Holdings rebranded as Casual Dining Group (CDG).{{cite news |last1=Gerrard |first1=Neil |title=Tragus Group renamed Casual Dining Group |url=https://www.thecaterer.com/news/restaurant/tragus-group-renamed-casual-dining-group |accessdate=29 May 2020 |work=The Caterer |date=3 March 2015}} In July 2015, CDG acquired [[Las Iguanas]]{{cite web|last1=Wallin|first1=James|title=Casual Dining Group acquires Las Iguanas|url=http://www.bighospitality.co.uk/Business/Casual-Dining-Group-acquires-Las-Iguanas|website=Big Hospitality|publisher=William Reed}} and later went on to purchase La Tasca.{{cite news|last1=Armstrong|first1=Ashley|title=Café Rouge owner seals La Tasca takeover just days after Las Iguanas deal|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/finance/newsbysector/retailandconsumer/11746702/Cafe-Rouge-owner-seals-La-Tasca-takeover-just-days-after-Las-Iguanas-deal.html|website=The Telegraph|date=18 July 2015|accessdate=8 August 2017}}{{cite news|author=Deirdre Hipwell |url=https://www.thetimes.com/travel/destinations/europe-travel/spain/dining-out-at-la-tasca-costs-group-tasty-pound25m-xdnps0dx9bv |title=Dining out at La Tasca costs group tasty £25m|work=[[The Times]]|date=2015-08-29 |access-date=2017-12-09}} CDG also opened concessions including Bella Italia, Café Rouge and Las Iguanas restaurants at Centre Parcs villages,{{cite web|last1=Seymour|first1=Andrew|title=Las Iguanas and Center Parcs venture into restaurant agreement|url=http://www.foodserviceequipmentjournal.com/las-iguanas-and-center-parcs-ventures-into-restaurant-agreement/|website=Foodservice Equipment Journal|date=12 September 2016|accessdate=2 March 2017}} and in UK airports, including [[Gatwick Airport|Gatwick]], [[Heathrow Airport|Heathrow]], [[Jersey Airport|Jersey]] and [[Inverness Airport|Inverness]].{{cite web|last1=Pigden|first1=Katey|title=Casual Dining Group to open Rapide at Inverness Airport|url=https://www.thecaterer.com/articles/368161/casual-dining-group-to-open-rapide-at-inverness-airport|website=The Caterer|date=17 August 2016|accessdate=2 March 2017}} However, efforts to close loss-making outlets and stem group losses continued through to 2018.{{cite news|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/business/2018/03/12/cost-hike-leads-deeper-losses-cafe-rouge-bella-italia-owner/|title=Cost hike leads to deeper losses at Cafe Rouge and Bella Italia owner|first=Bradley|last=Gerrard|newspaper=The Telegraph|date=12 March 2018|accessdate=3 June 2019|via=www.telegraph.co.uk}}{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/business-43371491|title=Cafe Rouge owner reports £60m loss|first=Bill|last=Wilson|work=BBC News|date=12 March 2018|accessdate=3 June 2019}} Also in 2018, Apollo sold its stake in the group to [[Kohlberg Kravis Roberts|KKR]] and Pemberton Capital Advisors (the two had provided loan finance since 2015).{{cite news |title=KKR-backed Casual Dining Group prepares to appoint administrators |url=http://deepinvesting.net/2020/05/19/kkr-backed-casual-dining-group-prepares-to-appoint-administrators/ |accessdate=8 June 2020 |work=Deep Investing |date=19 May 2020 |archive-date=8 June 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200608132308/http://deepinvesting.net/2020/05/19/kkr-backed-casual-dining-group-prepares-to-appoint-administrators/ |url-status=dead }} Some La Tasca restaurants were converted to other brands, and the remaining four La Tasca restaurants were sold in February 2020.{{Cite web|url=https://www.bighospitality.co.uk/Article/2020/02/21/Casual-Dining-Group-sells-off-final-four-La-Tasca-restaurant-sites|title=Casual Dining Group sells off final four La Tasca sites|website=bighospitality.co.uk}} [[File:Frankie and Benny's Newport - geograph.org.uk - 1439169.jpg|thumb|Frankie & Benny's in [[Newport, Wales]]. The Big Table bought the chain in 2023.]] On 18 May 2020, during the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom|COVID-19 pandemic]], CDG announced that it was working with advisors on next steps for the business as a prudent measure to protect the company whilst planning for the future.{{Cite web|url=https://www.casualdininggroup.com/noi/|title=Notice of Intention|website=Casual Dining Group}}{{Dead link|date=June 2021 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} Media reports suggested the group was preparing to place one of its three core brands into [[administration (law)|administration]] as part of a financial restructuring of the business.{{cite news |last1=McAllister |first1=James |title=Casual Dining Group in talks with creditors about restructuring |url=https://www.bighospitality.co.uk/Article/2020/05/18/Casual-Dining-Group-in-talks-with-creditors-about-radical-restructuring-Coronavirus-crisis |accessdate=29 May 2020 |work=Big Hospitality |date=18 May 2020}} On 29 May, CDG was reportedly in talks with "multiple parties", including other restaurant groups and private equity firms, over a sale of the business, potentially saving 6,000 jobs.{{cite news |last1=Gill |first1=Oliver |title=Cafe Rouge and Bella Italia owner in sale talks |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/business/2020/05/29/cafe-rouge-bella-italia-owner-sale-talks/ |accessdate=29 May 2020 |work=Telegraph |date=29 May 2020}} On 2 July 2020, it was announced that the company had been placed into administration, with 91 outlets set to close, with the loss of 1,900 jobs, leaving the group with 159 operational restaurants. They appointed [[AlixPartners]] to deal with the administration and said that the 91 outlets would be permanently shut as no buyers were offering to acquire them.{{Cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/business/2020/jul/02/bella-italia-owner-falls-into-administration-with-loss-of-1900-jobs|title=Bella Italia owner falls into administration, with loss of 1,900 jobs|work=The Guardian|last=Wood|first=Zoe|date=2 July 2020|access-date=2 July 2020}} ===The Big Table=== On 3 August 2020, it was announced that Casual Dining Group, including the Las Iguanas, Bella Italia and Café Rouge restaurants, had been acquired out of administration by private equity firm Epiris and rebranded as The Big Table, led by the existing management team under CEO James Spragg.{{cite web |last1=McAllister |first1=James |title=Casual Dining Group rebrands as The Big Table after being acquired by former TGI Friday's backer |url=https://www.bighospitality.co.uk/Article/2020/08/03/Casual-Dining-Group-rebrands-as-The-Big-Table-acquired-by-Epiris-Bella-Italia-Cafe-Rouge-Coronavirus |website=Big Hospitality |access-date=29 January 2021 |date=3 August 2020}} In 2023, The Big Table bought most of [[The Restaurant Group]]'s loss-making assets for £7.5 million.{{Cite web |title=The Big Table Group Limited acquired of 75 Frankie & Benny's and Chiquito Restaurants from The Restaurant Group plc. |url=https://in.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/RESTAURANT-GROUP-9590109/news/The-Big-Table-Group-Limited-acquired-of-75-Frankie-Benny-s-and-Chiquito-Restaurants-from-The-Resta-45188083/ |access-date=2024-01-12 |work=MarketScreener |language=en}}{{Cite web |title=The Big Table Group {{!}} Home - The Big Table Group |url=https://www.bigtablegroup.com/ |access-date=2024-04-03 |website=www.bigtablegroup.com}} ==Social responsibility== CDG claimed to emphasise [[corporate social responsibility]] practices.{{cite web|url=https://www.casualdininggroup.com/csr/|title=Casual Dining Group - Operator of some of the UK's favourite restaurant brands|website=www.casualdininggroup.com|accessdate=3 June 2019|archive-date=10 April 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190410185342/https://www.casualdininggroup.com/csr/|url-status=dead}} It reduced its energy consumption by 17% from 2012 to 2016,{{cite web|last1=Carol|first1=Millet|title=Casual Dining Group cuts restaurant energy waste|url=https://www.thecaterer.com/articles/366325/casual-dining-group-cuts-restaurant-energy-waste|website=The Caterer|date=17 March 2016|accessdate=2 March 2017}} and had a partnership with [[The Prince's Trust]] charity.{{cite web|last1=Mellor|first1=Charlotte|title=Casual Dining Group partners with Princes Trust|url=http://www.casualdiningmagazine.co.uk/news/2016-08-05-casual-dining-group-partners-with-the-princes-trust|website=Casual Dining Magazine|accessdate=2 March 2017|archive-date=3 March 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170303122611/http://www.casualdiningmagazine.co.uk/news/2016-08-05-casual-dining-group-partners-with-the-princes-trust|url-status=dead}} Some CDG brands ranked highly for seafood sustainability (within their class).{{cite web|title=Lack of clarity on the menu leaves diners in the dark when making a seafood choice|url=http://fish2fork.com/en_GB/news/news/lack-of-clarity-on-the-menu-leaves-diners-in-the-dark-when-making-a-seafood-choice|accessdate=2 March 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170303050055/http://fish2fork.com/en_GB/news/news/lack-of-clarity-on-the-menu-leaves-diners-in-the-dark-when-making-a-seafood-choice|archive-date=3 March 2017|url-status=dead}} All whole eggs sourced by the company for its kitchens were [[Free-range eggs|free-range]] together with eggs used as ingredients for sauces and pasta. In 2016, in partnership with [[Compassion in World Farming]], CDG said it aimed to use solely free-range eggs as ingredients by 2025.{{cite web|url=https://www.caterlyst.com/c3t/insight/Sector.aspx?t=13&n=14528#sthash.BgsnUJG5.dpuf |title=Data |publisher=www.caterlyst.com |accessdate=2020-02-05}} In 2019, CDG signed up to the [[European Chicken Commitment]] to improve chicken welfare.{{cite web |title=Casual Dining Group commits to improved chicken welfare (12 August 2019) |url=https://www.foodspark.com/Hot-Topics/Casual-Dining-Group-commits-to-improved-chicken-welfare |website=Foodspark |accessdate=30 May 2020 }}{{Dead link|date=November 2023 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} CDG had a partnership with UK charity [[FareShare]] to redistribute food that would go to waste to people in need instead.{{cite web|url=https://fareshare.org.uk/giving-food/who-we-work-with/our-work-with-casual-dining-group/|title=Our Work With Casual Dining Group|website=FareShare|language=en-GB|access-date=2019-07-12}} ==Controversy== In 2009 Tragus was the subject of newspaper reports highlighting the practice of several UK restaurant chains using customer tips to meet [[minimum wage]] laws for waiters/waitresses. The company's business model was said to depend on paying servers as little as £2.50 an hour, with the rest coming as tips.Jamie Elliott, [https://www.theguardian.com/money/2009/jun/07/waiters-tips-restaurants-minimum-wage "Tip off: waiters still paid minimum wage out of your service charge"], ''Guardian'' 7 June 2009 The company reportedly instructed restaurant managers to pressure servers to avoid encouraging customers to give tips in cash, which would not count as part of wages, and was threatening to sack employees who failed to produce a sufficient volume of card-based gratuities. They were discovered (via "mystery diners") informing customers of the company's policy.Jamie Elliott, [https://www.theguardian.com/lifeandstyle/2009/jun/28/restaurant-chains-scare-tactics-gratuities "Cafe waiters fear the axe over cash tips"], ''Guardian'', 28 June 2009 When the practice became unlawful on 1 October 2009, Tragus reviewed and updated its policies to ensure that all tips, after a 10% deduction for administrative and other costs paid by credit or debit card, were distributed through the payroll system to restaurant staff via a [[Gratuity#Tronc|Tronc]] system. In 2020, Casual Dining Group policy was that all customer cash tips and service charges were kept by restaurant employees in full.{{Cite web|title=People|url=https://www.casualdininggroup.com/csr/people/|access-date=2020-06-02|website=Casual Dining Group|language=en-GB|archive-date=27 July 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190727131250/https://www.casualdininggroup.com/csr/people/|url-status=dead}}{{efn|When tips or service charge are paid for by a credit card or debit card, the company makes a 2.5% administration charge to cover bank fees, before distributing the remainder in full to employees. Tips and service charges are paid in full in addition to the National Minimum Wage and National Living Wage. Any tips paid in cash are retained by the individual waiter. It is the responsibility of those receiving cash tips to declare the income for tax purposes to HM Revenue & Customs.}} ==Notes== {{notelist}} ==References== {{reflist}} {{Blackstone Companies}} {{KKR}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Big Table Group, the}} [[Category:Companies that have entered administration in the United Kingdom]] [[Category:KKR & Co. companies]] [[Category:Privately held companies of the United Kingdom]] [[Category:Restaurant chains in the United Kingdom]] [[Category:2014 establishments in England]]
extract:
The Big Table Group Limited, formerly Tragus Group and Casual Dining Group (CDG), is a hospitality company in the United Kingdom. The Big Table operates restaurants primarily under the Bella Italia, Café Rouge, Frankie & Benny's and Las Iguanas names. It also operates sites under the Banana Tree, Chiquito, Coast to Coast, Firejacks and Filling Station brands. It is owned by Epiris.
In mid-May 2020, CDG warned its chains were at risk of going into administration but was later in talks with "multiple parties" about a sale of the business. On 2 July 2020, it was announced that the company had been placed into administration, with 91 outlets set to close with the loss of 1,900 jobs.
Epiris brought CDG out of administration in August 2020, renaming it to The Big Table Group.
